title: Thoryn CLI connection contract
description: SSO-2948 (epic SSO-2947) — a schema-backed, declarative sign-in configuration for the `thoryn` CLI: HOW a caller (a person for their own use cases, or a CI pipeline dogfooding the same feature) signs the CLI into a given workspace/identity. It is DATA, not code — a sibling of the recipe schema — passed to `thoryn login --connection <file>`. The workspace slug derives the per-tenant issuer (`https://<slug>.<label>.<env>`) and gateway. Two auth methods, one per client: `client_credentials` (an API key — the SECRET is NEVER in this file, only the NAME of the environment variable that carries it, `auth.secretEnv`) and, since SSO-3308, `workload_identity` (a GitHub Actions workload identity trust — no secret at all: the job's own OIDC token is exchanged, so the file names no env var). A client id is public and MAY appear.

workspace.description: The workspace this CLI binds to. Its slug derives the per-tenant hub issuer and gateway.

slug.description: Workspace slug (same grammar as a recipe workspace slug). Derives https://<slug>.hub.<env>.

hubBaseUrlEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the platform BASE ISSUER (e.g. https://auth.stg.thoryn.org). The per-workspace issuer is derived by prefixing the slug on that host, reusing whatever host label it carries (SSO-3296). Defaults to THORYN_HUB, which also accepts the documented THORYN_ISSUER spelling; when unset the CLI's baked-in default is used.

auth.description: How the CLI authenticates into the workspace. `client_credentials` needs `secretEnv`; `workload_identity` must not carry one.

method.description: Authentication method: `client_credentials` (an API key, secret named by `secretEnv`) or `workload_identity` (SSO-3308 — a GitHub Actions job exchanges its OIDC token under a workload identity trust; runs only inside a job with `permissions: id-token: write`).

clientId.description: OAuth client id of the machine client — for `workload_identity` the trust's `clientId` (`wi_…`). PUBLIC — a client id is not a secret and MAY be committed.

secretEnv.description: `client_credentials` only (required there): NAME of the environment variable holding the client secret (a GitHub secret in CI; a locally-exported var for a developer). NEVER the secret value itself.

scopes.description: The EXACT scope set requested — the ceiling AND the floor (the platform grants only what is requested). Non-empty, unique, each a tenant:<resource>.<verb> scope. For `workload_identity`, a subset of the trust's scopes.

provider.description: `workload_identity` only: the workload identity provider. `github_actions` is the only provider (the default).

audience.description: `workload_identity` only: the trust's `audience` EXACTLY (as `thoryn workload-identity trusts create|get` prints it) — the audience the job requests its OIDC token for. When omitted it is derived: the workspace issuer, plus `/<environment>` for a sandbox. Required when the workspace has an active custom domain.

environment.description: `workload_identity` only, and only when `audience` is omitted: the slug of the sandbox environment the trust lives in; the derived audience becomes <workspace issuer>/<environment>. Omit for a production-plane trust.

tokenEndpoint.description: `workload_identity` only: the trust's `tokenEndpoint`. Default `<audience>/oauth2/token`. Must be on the audience's own origin — the CLI refuses to send a job token anywhere else.

github.description: `workload_identity` only, optional: the trust's GitHub pins (same names as the trust API's `github`). Used ONLY to explain a refused sign-in — the platform refuses every mismatch with the same `invalid_client`, so the CLI compares the job's claims with these and names the field that differs. They grant nothing; the trust on the platform decides.

environment.description: The GitHub environment the job must run in (exact).

ref.description: The exact `ref` the job must run on.

githubHostedRunnersOnly.description: The trust accepts only GitHub-hosted runners.
